newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-CAMPBELL PUTS ZIMBABWE IN COMMAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAMPBELL PUTS ZIMBABWE IN COMMAND.

text.p: Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell put his side in command on the first day of the inaugural test against England on Wednesday with a bright 84 after winning the toss and electing to bat.
At tea Zimbabwe were 200 for three with Dave Houghton on 33 and Andy Flower on 31.
England fast bowler Darren Gough made an early breakthrough on a steamy morning by dismissing Stuart Carlisle for a third ball duck, well caught by John Crawley at short-leg.
Left-hander Campbell took the attack to the bowlers, reaching 70 out of 109 for one at lunch with 11 fours from 102 balls.

After the interval, Campbell and Grant Flower took their second wicket stand to 127 before England debutant Chris Silverwood broke the partnership when he found the edge of Flower's bat. Nasser Hussain took an outstanding catch at third slip to dispose of the opener for a gritty 43 off 99 balls.
The prize wicket of Campbell fell three overs later to the deserving Robert Croft. The off-spinner drew Campbell into a drive which sliced off the outside edge to Silverwood at point.
Campbell's innings had included 13 boundaries and came off 137 balls.
After an edgy start the fourth wicket pair of Houghton and Andy Flower stabilised the innings. Flower brought up the 200 with a lofted on-drive for four from the final ball before the interval.
